lead.title: UCL spin-out Octopath AI raises £1.5M seed (Twin Path Ventures) for single-cell AI pathology
lead.deck: Two foundation models — Kraken for H&E slides, Nemo for IHC — analyse routine slides at single-cell resolution in under two minutes (cellularity, immune infiltration, mitotic counts), with results left for pathologist review. The round combines a seed led by Twin Path Ventures with a matched Innovate UK grant; funds target clinical evaluation, product development and the regulatory pathway.

word.fr: Computational pathology: deep-learning analysis of digitised tissue slides to assist diagnosis and predict clinical endpoints.
word.definition: The biopsy slide is scanned into a giant image, then an AI reads it to help the pathologist spot cancer cells and anticipate disease course or treatment response.

parts.label: Digitised slide (whole-slide image)
parts.role: The tissue slide is scanned into an image of several billion pixels, the raw material for the algorithms.

parts.label: Deep learning
parts.role: Neural networks, the core algorithmic component of most systems, analyse the image (e.g. via multiple-instance learning).

parts.label: Predicted clinical endpoint
parts.role: The model outputs a diagnostic aid or a prediction of a clinical endpoint, even new morphological biomarkers.

how.t: Pathology slides are digitised into high-resolution images, making analysis automatable.
Deep-learning models scan the whole image to detect, count or classify structures such as tumour cells.
Results serve as decision support; some AI systems are now approved to assist clinical diagnosis, but technical barriers to adoption remain.

word.why: VC angle: slide digitisation creates a data bottleneck that AI can monetise, on the diagnostic side and the pharma side (drug-development support). The market is still young: recent European rounds are modest (£1.5M at Octopath AI, $15.3M at Mindpeak) and Aiforia's EIB venture debt shows partly non-dilutive financing. Risks: long clinical and regulatory validation, slow adoption, need for large and varied datasets.

startups.name: Octopath AI
startups.use: UCL spin-out; Kraken and Nemo foundation models analysing routine slides at cellular resolution in under two minutes, trained on over 14 million annotated cells across 14 cancer types; £1.5M seed + grant (incl. £500k Innovate UK) led by TwinPath Ventures, deployed at five sites including UCLH.

startups.name: Mindpeak
startups.use: AI software for pathologists (breast cancer, PD-L1, etc.); $15.3M Series A announced October 2, 2024, led by ZEISS Ventures and IFB Innovationsstarter with InnoVentureFonds, AI.FUND and the EIC Fund; over 30,000 diagnoses supported; no acquisition found.

startups.name: Aiforia
startups.use: Deep-learning AI software for pathology, listed on Nasdaq First North Helsinki; €20M EIB venture debt (InvestEU) in three tranches, a first of €5M, announced July 31, 2026.
